back: It's on me! My treat!
definition: A common formula for announcing that you will pay for everyone.
examples: Mettete via i portafogli, stasera offro io!
examples_en: Put your wallets away, tonight it's on me!

back: on foot, walking
definition: Used to say you go somewhere by walking rather than by vehicle.
examples: Preferisco andare in centro a piedi.
examples_en: I prefer to go downtown on foot.

back: see you soon
definition: A friendly farewell when you expect to meet or talk again before long.
examples: Grazie della visita, a presto!
examples_en: Thanks for visiting, see you soon!

back: to visit, to drop in on
definition: Used for visiting a friend or relative at their home.
examples: Domenica andiamo a trovare i nonni.
examples_en: On Sunday we're going to visit Grandma and Grandpa.

back: congratulations, best wishes
definition: Used for birthdays, holidays and other occasions when you wish someone well.
examples: Auguri per il tuo compleanno!
examples_en: Best wishes for your birthday!

back: to need
definition: The usual way to say you need something or need to do something.
examples: Ho bisogno di un po' di riposo.
examples_en: I need a bit of rest.

back: to be in a hurry
definition: Used to say you must do something quickly or have little time.
examples: Scusami, ho fretta: devo prendere il treno.
examples_en: Sorry, I'm in a hurry: I have to catch the train.

back: to be right
definition: The standard way to say someone is correct; its opposite is 'avere torto'. Italian uses 'avere', not 'essere'.
examples: Hai ragione, scusami: ho sbagliato io.
examples_en: You're right, sorry, I was the one who got it wrong.

back: to be wrong
definition: Means being mistaken; the opposite of 'avere ragione'.
examples: Ammetto che avevo torto io.
examples_en: I admit I was the one who was wrong.

back: to feel like
definition: Used to express a wish or mood for doing or having something.
examples: Stasera non ho voglia di uscire.
examples_en: Tonight I don't feel like going out.

back: enjoy your meal
definition: Said before eating, to people at your table or to those who are about to eat.
examples: Buon appetito a tutti!
examples_en: Enjoy your meal, everyone!

back: have a good trip
definition: Wished to someone who is leaving or traveling.
examples: Buon viaggio e a presto!
examples_en: Have a good trip and see you soon!

back: have a good day
definition: A common way to say goodbye in the morning or during the day.
examples: Grazie e buona giornata!
examples_en: Thank you and have a good day!

back: what's up? what's wrong?
definition: Asked when someone seems upset or when you want to know what's going on.
examples: Hai una faccia strana: che c'è?
examples_en: You look odd: what's wrong?

back: who knows, I wonder
definition: Expresses uncertainty or wondering about something, often said to yourself.
examples: Chissà se Marco viene alla festa.
examples_en: I wonder if Marco is coming to the party.

back: see you around
definition: A casual goodbye among friends and colleagues.
examples: Devo andare, ci vediamo domani!
examples_en: I have to go, see you tomorrow!

back: how come, why
definition: A friendly way of asking the reason for something surprising.
examples: Come mai sei già a casa?
examples_en: How come you're home already?

back: okay, agreed
definition: Used to accept a proposal or say you agree.
examples: Ci vediamo alle otto? — D'accordo.
examples_en: Shall we meet at eight? Okay.

back: usually, as a rule
definition: Introduces what normally or habitually happens.
examples: Di solito mi alzo alle sette.
examples_en: Usually I get up at seven.

back: to go grocery shopping
definition: The standard way to say you are buying food and household goods.
examples: Domani devo fare la spesa al supermercato.
examples_en: Tomorrow I have to go grocery shopping at the supermarket.

back: to go for a stroll or a ride, to look around
definition: Used for a casual outing on foot, by bike or by car, with no fixed destination.
examples: Dopo cena facciamo un giro in centro?
examples_en: Shall we take a walk downtown after dinner?

back: thanks a lot
definition: A very common, warm way to thank someone.
examples: Grazie mille per l'aiuto!
examples_en: Thanks a lot for the help!

back: break a leg, good luck
definition: Said to wish someone luck before an exam, performance or challenge; the standard reply is 'Crepi!'.
examples: Domani hai l'esame? In bocca al lupo!
examples_en: You have your exam tomorrow? Break a leg!

back: better late than never
definition: Said when something happens late, to say it is still good that it happened.
examples: Finalmente hai chiamato, meglio tardi che mai!
examples_en: You finally called, better late than never!

back: thank goodness, what a relief
definition: Said when something turns out better than feared, expressing relief.
examples: Meno male che hai preso l'ombrello!
examples_en: Thank goodness you took the umbrella!

back: excuse me, I'm sorry
definition: Formal way to get attention, pass by someone or apologize.
examples: Mi scusi, è libero questo posto?
examples_en: Excuse me, is this seat free?

back: it's okay, no problem
definition: A common reply to an apology, meaning there is no harm done.
examples: Scusa se ho rotto il bicchiere. — Non fa niente.
examples_en: Sorry I broke the glass. It's okay.

back: never mind, it doesn't matter
definition: Used to dismiss a problem or reassure someone that something is not important.
examples: Sei in ritardo? Non importa, ti aspetto.
examples_en: You're late? Never mind, I'll wait for you.

back: I can't wait
definition: Used to say you are very eager for something to happen, usually followed by 'di' + infinitive.
examples: Non vedo l'ora di partire per le vacanze.
examples_en: I can't wait to leave for vacation.

back: once in a while
definition: A very common way to say something happens occasionally.
examples: Ogni tanto mi chiama ancora.
examples_en: He still calls me once in a while.

back: by chance, by any chance
definition: Used for something happening accidentally, or to politely ask a question.
examples: Hai per caso visto le mie chiavi?
examples_en: Have you seen my keys by any chance?

back: please
definition: The standard way to make a polite request.
examples: Mi porta il conto, per favore?
examples_en: Could you bring me the check, please?

back: luckily, fortunately
definition: Introduces a good outcome that could have gone otherwise.
examples: Per fortuna ho preso l'ombrello.
examples_en: Luckily I took my umbrella.

back: not at all
definition: An emphatic negation, often used in answers.
examples: Il film non mi è piaciuto per niente.
examples_en: I didn't like the movie at all.

back: to waste time
definition: Used when spending time on something useless or delaying unnecessarily.
examples: Non perdiamo tempo, siamo già in ritardo.
examples_en: Let's not waste time, we're already late.

back: nice to meet you
definition: Said when being introduced to someone for the first time.
examples: Piacere, sono Marco.
examples_en: Nice to meet you, I'm Marco.

back: you're welcome / please, go ahead
definition: Used to answer thanks, or to invite someone to go first, come in or sit down.
examples: — Grazie mille! — Prego!
examples_en: "Thanks a lot!" "You're welcome!"

back: sooner or later
definition: Says that something will certainly happen eventually, even if the time is uncertain.
examples: Prima o poi dovrai dirglielo.
examples_en: Sooner or later you'll have to tell him.

back: maybe, it could be
definition: A common way to admit something is possible without committing to it.
examples: Può darsi che abbia ragione lui.
examples_en: Maybe he's right.

back: bless you / cheers
definition: Said after someone sneezes, or as a toast when drinking.
examples: Hai starnutito? Salute!
examples_en: You sneezed? Bless you!

back: in my opinion, if you ask me
definition: The most common way to introduce your own opinion in conversation.
examples: Secondo me hai fatto la scelta giusta.
examples_en: I think you made the right choice.

back: don't worry, relax
definition: Used to reassure someone; 'stia tranquillo' is the formal form.
examples: Stai tranquillo, ci penso io.
examples_en: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.

back: seriously, for real
definition: Used to stress that you mean something or to ask if it's true.
examples: Dici sul serio? Non ci credo!
examples_en: Are you serious? I don't believe it!

back: no worries, take it easy
definition: Used to reassure someone that there's no problem or no need to worry (feminine: 'tranquilla').
examples: Tranquillo, ci penso io a tutto.
examples_en: No worries, I'll take care of everything.

back: to tell the truth, actually
definition: Introduces a frank statement, often one that slightly contradicts what was expected.
examples: A dire il vero, non mi piace molto il caffè.
examples_en: To tell the truth, I don't really like coffee.

back: very close, just around the corner
definition: Used to say a place is very near, usually walking distance.
examples: La stazione è a due passi da qui.
examples_en: The station is just around the corner from here.

back: by the way, speaking of which
definition: Introduces a related topic or a thing you've just remembered. Don't confuse it with 'di proposito' (on purpose).
examples: A proposito, hai sentito Marco di recente?
examples_en: By the way, have you talked to Marco recently?

back: one hundred percent
definition: Used to express complete certainty or total commitment.
examples: Sono sicuro al cento per cento.
examples_en: I'm one hundred percent sure.

back: suddenly
definition: Describes something happening without warning.
examples: All'improvviso è saltata la corrente.
examples_en: Suddenly the power went out.

back: in the end
definition: Introduces the final outcome after a process or hesitation.
examples: Alla fine abbiamo deciso di restare a casa.
examples_en: In the end we decided to stay home.

back: to your health, cheers
definition: A toast said when raising glasses; the formal version is 'alla sua salute', and 'alla salute' works for everyone.
examples: Alla tua salute, e a questa serata!
examples_en: To your health, and to this evening!

back: to get along
definition: Used to say that two people have a good relationship and don't argue.
examples: Mia suocera e io andiamo molto d'accordo.
examples_en: My mother-in-law and I get along really well.

back: to leave, to go away
definition: Means to depart, often abruptly or definitively.
examples: Se n'è andato senza salutare.
examples_en: He left without saying goodbye.

back: to have goosebumps
definition: Used for goosebumps caused by cold, fear or strong emotion.
examples: Quella canzone mi fa venire la pelle d'oca.
examples_en: That song gives me goosebumps.

back: to change the subject
definition: Used when someone steers the conversation away from an uncomfortable topic.
examples: Quando ho chiesto dei soldi, ha cambiato discorso.
examples_en: When I asked about the money, he changed the subject.

front: chi va piano va sano e va lontano
lemma: chi va piano va sano e va lontano
back: slow and steady wins the race
definition: Advice to be patient and careful, because hurrying leads to mistakes and accidents.
literal: who goes slowly goes safely and goes far
examples: Non correre con il progetto: chi va piano va sano e va lontano.
examples_en: Don't rush the project: slow and steady wins the race.

back: it takes, you need
definition: Expresses the time, amount or thing required; becomes 'ci vogliono' with plurals.
examples: Ci vuole un'ora per arrivare in aeroporto.
examples_en: It takes an hour to get to the airport.

back: may I come in? / excuse me (to pass)
definition: Said when entering someone's home or squeezing past people.
examples: Con permesso, posso entrare?
examples_en: Excuse me, may I come in?

back: thanks! (reply to 'good luck')
definition: The standard reply to 'In bocca al lupo!', short for 'Crepi il lupo!'.
examples: — In bocca al lupo per l'esame! — Crepi!
examples_en: "Good luck on the exam!" "Thanks!"

back: thanks (reply to 'good luck')
definition: The traditional response to 'in bocca al lupo', often shortened to 'Crepi!'.
examples: — In bocca al lupo! — Crepi!
examples_en: "Break a leg!" "Thanks!"

back: to bother, to annoy
definition: Used when something or someone irritates or disturbs you; also in polite requests.
examples: Ti dà fastidio se apro la finestra?
examples_en: Does it bother you if I open the window?

back: to give a ride
definition: Used when offering to take someone somewhere in your car or on your scooter.
examples: Se vuoi, ti do un passaggio fino alla stazione.
examples_en: If you want, I'll give you a ride to the station.

back: to get busy, to roll up one's sleeves and get going
definition: Used to urge or describe someone who actively takes initiative and works hard to get something done.
examples: Se vuoi trovare lavoro, devi darti da fare.
examples_en: If you want to find a job, you have to get busy.

back: for sure, certainly
definition: Used to say you are confident something is or will be true.
examples: Domani di sicuro piove, guarda il cielo.
examples_en: It will definitely rain tomorrow, look at the sky.

back: to fight like cats and dogs
definition: Describes two people who constantly argue or can't get along.
literal: to be like dog and cat
examples: I due fratelli sono sempre stati come cane e gatto.
examples_en: The two brothers have always fought like cats and dogs.

back: to feel low, to be down in the dumps
definition: A common way to say someone is sad or discouraged.
examples: Oggi sono un po' giù di morale.
examples_en: I'm feeling a bit down today.

back: to be on sale
definition: Said of items that are discounted, especially during the seasonal sales (i saldi).
literal: to be in sale (saldo = balance, clearance)
examples: Le scarpe sono in saldo fino a sabato.
examples_en: The shoes are on sale until Saturday.

back: to be in trouble
definition: Used when someone is in a difficult or risky situation, often because of a mistake.
examples: Se il capo scopre l'errore, siamo nei guai.
examples_en: If the boss finds out about the mistake, we're in trouble.

back: to be fed up with
definition: Used when you've had enough of something or someone.
literal: to be sick and tired of
examples: Sono stufo di aspettare l'autobus ogni mattina.
examples_en: I'm fed up with waiting for the bus every morning.

back: to have a little chat
definition: Used for an informal, relaxed conversation, often with no particular purpose.
examples: Passa da me domani, facciamo due chiacchiere.
examples_en: Come by tomorrow, we'll have a little chat.

back: to take a short walk, to go for a stroll
definition: Means going for a relaxed short walk, often after a meal or to clear your head.
examples: Dopo cena facciamo due passi in centro?
examples_en: After dinner, shall we take a stroll downtown?

back: to pretend to
definition: Followed by an infinitive, it means acting as if something were true when it isn't.
examples: Ha fatto finta di non vedermi.
examples_en: He pretended not to see me.

back: to fill up the tank
definition: Used at the gas station to say you fill the car's tank completely. Also figuratively, e.g. fare il pieno di energia.
examples: Prima di partire dobbiamo fare il pieno.
examples_en: Before leaving we have to fill up the tank.

back: to stand in line, to queue
definition: Used for waiting in a line, at the store, post office and so on.
examples: Abbiamo fatto la fila per mezz'ora.
examples_en: We stood in line for half an hour.

back: to make up, to make peace
definition: Used when people reconcile after an argument.
examples: Dai, fate pace e smettetela di litigare!
examples_en: Come on, make up and stop fighting!

back: to get a bargain, to make a good deal
definition: Used when you buy something at a very good price.
examples: Con questo televisore ho fatto un affare.
examples_en: I got a great deal on this TV.

back: to stop by, to pop in
definition: Used for a quick, informal visit to a person or place.
examples: Domani faccio un salto da te dopo il lavoro.
examples_en: Tomorrow I'll stop by your place after work.

back: early, ahead of time
definition: Used for arriving or doing something before the expected time.
examples: Sono arrivata in anticipo all'appuntamento.
examples_en: I got to the appointment early.

back: don't judge a book by its cover
definition: Said to warn that appearances can be misleading and a person's clothes don't show who they really are.
literal: the habit doesn't make the monk
examples: Sembra severo, ma è dolcissimo: l'abito non fa il monaco.
examples_en: He seems strict, but he's very sweet: don't judge a book by its cover.

back: there's strength in numbers
definition: Said to stress that people achieve more when they work together.
examples: Dobbiamo collaborare: l'unione fa la forza.
examples_en: We have to cooperate: there's strength in numbers.

back: never say never
definition: A saying used to remind that nothing is completely impossible.
examples: Io in montagna? Mai dire mai!
examples_en: Me, in the mountains? Never say never!

back: to set aside, to save up
definition: Used for saving money for the future or for a goal.
examples: Ogni mese metto da parte cento euro.
examples_en: Every month I put aside a hundred euros.

back: it's worth it
definition: Used to say an effort, cost or trouble is justified by the result.
literal: of it the effort is worth
examples: È lontano, ma ne vale la pena.
examples_en: It's far, but it's worth it.

back: you're welcome, don't mention it
definition: A polite reply to thanks, a bit more formal than 'prego'.
examples: Grazie mille per l'aiuto! — Non c'è di che.
examples_en: Thanks so much for the help! You're welcome.

back: I can't manage it, I can't take it
definition: Used when you lack the strength, time or patience to do something.
examples: Non ce la faccio più, sono stanchissimo.
examples_en: I can't go on any longer, I'm exhausted.

back: to be unable to wait, to look forward to something
definition: Used to express eager anticipation of an event, usually followed by 'di' + infinitive.
examples: Non vedo l'ora di partire per le vacanze.
examples_en: I can't wait to leave for vacation.

front: non è tutto oro quel che luccica
lemma: non è tutto oro quel che luccica
back: all that glitters is not gold
definition: Warns that something attractive may not be as good as it looks.
literal: it's not all gold that glitters
examples: Quel lavoro sembra perfetto, ma non è tutto oro quel che luccica.
examples_en: That job seems perfect, but all that glitters is not gold.

back: rush hour
definition: Used for the busiest times of day on roads and public transport.
examples: All'ora di punta la metro è piena di gente.
examples_en: During rush hour the subway is packed.

back: for now, for the time being
definition: Used for a situation that is valid now but may change.
examples: Per il momento non ho bisogno di aiuto.
examples_en: For the time being I don't need any help.

back: to miss the train, to miss the boat
definition: Used literally for missing transport, and figuratively for missing an opportunity.
examples: Se non ti iscrivi subito, rischi di perdere il treno.
examples_en: If you don't sign up right away, you risk missing the boat.

back: to tease, to make fun of
definition: Used for teasing someone, either playfully among friends or in a more mocking way.
examples: I miei fratelli mi prendono sempre in giro per il mio accento.
examples_en: My brothers are always teasing me about my accent.

back: to realize
definition: Used when you become aware of something; followed by 'di' or 'che'.
examples: Mi sono reso conto di aver sbagliato strada.
examples_en: I realized I'd taken the wrong road.

back: sorry to bother you
definition: A polite phrase used when interrupting or asking something of someone.
examples: Scusi il disturbo, sa dov'è la stazione?
examples_en: Sorry to bother you, do you know where the station is?

back: if I'm not mistaken
definition: Softens a statement when you are fairly but not completely sure.
literal: if I don't make a mistake
examples: Se non sbaglio, la riunione è alle tre.
examples_en: If I'm not mistaken, the meeting is at three.

back: without a doubt, undoubtedly
definition: Affirms something firmly, often when agreeing or giving an opinion.
examples: È senza dubbio il miglior ristorante della città.
examples_en: It's without a doubt the best restaurant in town.

back: to be about to
definition: Followed by an infinitive, it indicates something imminent.
examples: Stavo per uscire quando hai chiamato.
examples_en: I was about to go out when you called.

back: all good, everything's fine
definition: A common reply or question to check that things are in order.
examples: Allora, tutto a posto con i documenti?
examples_en: So, is everything all set with the documents?

back: roughly, more or less (as an estimate)
definition: Used when giving a rough estimate of an amount, time or distance.
examples: A occhio e croce ci vogliono due ore.
examples_en: Roughly speaking, it takes two hours.

back: apparently, it seems
definition: Reports something you have heard or inferred but are not certain of.
examples: A quanto pare, Luca non viene alla festa.
examples_en: Apparently, Luca isn't coming to the party.

back: mum's the word; keep it secret
definition: Said to tell someone not to reveal a secret or a piece of news.
examples: Domani c'è una sorpresa per Luca: acqua in bocca!
examples_en: Tomorrow there's a surprise for Luca: mum's the word!

back: great, awesomely
definition: Used to say that something is going or went very well.
examples: — Come va il nuovo lavoro? — Alla grande!
examples_en: "How's the new job?" "Great!"

back: to get up on the wrong side of the bed
definition: Used when someone is in a bad mood for no apparent reason.
literal: to get up with the wrong foot
examples: Oggi ti sei alzato con il piede sbagliato, eh?
examples_en: You got up on the wrong side of the bed today, huh?

back: to make ends meet
definition: Used when talking about having enough money to last until the next paycheck.
literal: to arrive at the end of the month
examples: Oggi è difficile arrivare a fine mese.
examples_en: Nowadays it's hard to make ends meet.

back: to be mad at someone, to have a grudge against someone
definition: Used when you are angry or resentful toward a person.
examples: Ce l'hai con me per ieri sera?
examples_en: Are you mad at me about last night?

back: to get chills
definition: Used for strong emotion, fear or excitement that makes you shiver.
examples: Ho i brividi ogni volta che sento quella canzone.
examples_en: I get chills every time I hear that song.

back: to be down-to-earth
definition: Said of a realistic, practical person who isn't carried away by fantasies.
literal: to have one's feet on the ground
examples: Per fortuna Giulia ha i piedi per terra.
examples_en: Luckily Giulia is down-to-earth.

back: to have one's doubts
definition: A polite way to say you are skeptical about something.
examples: Ho i miei dubbi che sia vero.
examples_en: I have my doubts that it's true.

back: to feel down
definition: Used when someone is discouraged or depressed.
literal: to have the morale on the ground
examples: Dopo la sconfitta avevamo tutti il morale a terra.
examples_en: After the defeat we were all feeling down.

back: to have a green thumb
definition: Said of someone who is very good at growing plants.
examples: Mia nonna ha il pollice verde: il balcone è una giungla.
examples_en: My grandmother has a green thumb: her balcony is a jungle.

back: to have one's mouth water
definition: Used when food (or something desirable) makes you crave it.
literal: to have the little water in the mouth
examples: Con questo profumo di ragù ho già l'acquolina in bocca.
examples_en: With this smell of ragù my mouth is already watering.

back: to be stubborn
definition: Describes someone who won't change their mind or listen to advice.
examples: Ha la testa dura, non ascolta mai nessuno.
examples_en: He's so stubborn, he never listens to anyone.

front: avere la testa fra le nuvole
lemma: avere la testa fra le nuvole
back: to have one's head in the clouds
definition: Describes someone absent-minded or dreamy; 'tra le nuvole' is equally common.
literal: to have the head among the clouds
examples: Scusa, oggi ho la testa fra le nuvole.
examples_en: Sorry, I have my head in the clouds today.

back: to have a good head on one's shoulders
definition: Said of a sensible, responsible person.
literal: to have one's head on one's shoulders
examples: Mia figlia è giovane ma ha la testa sulle spalle.
examples_en: My daughter is young but has a good head on her shoulders.

front: avere la testa tra le nuvole
lemma: avere la testa tra le nuvole
back: to have one's head in the clouds
definition: Said of someone distracted or dreamy.
literal: to have the head among the clouds
examples: Scusa, avevo la testa tra le nuvole.
examples_en: Sorry, I had my head in the clouds.

back: to spend money like water
definition: Said of someone who spends money too freely and can't save.
literal: to have holes in one's hands
examples: Marco ha le mani bucate: a metà mese è già senza soldi.
examples_en: Marco spends money like water: by mid-month he's already broke.

back: to have a heart of gold
definition: Said of a very kind, generous and caring person.
literal: to have a heart of gold
examples: La mia vicina ha un cuore d'oro: aiuta tutti.
examples_en: My neighbor has a heart of gold: she helps everyone.

back: to be ravenous, to be starving
definition: Said when you are extremely hungry.
literal: to have a hunger of wolves
examples: Dopo la partita avevamo una fame da lupi.
examples_en: After the game we were ravenous.

back: to have a memory like an elephant
definition: Said of someone who remembers everything, even small details.
literal: to have a memory of an elephant
examples: Non provare a mentirmi: ho una memoria da elefante.
examples_en: Don't try to lie to me: I have a memory like an elephant.

back: to be totally surprised, to be caught completely off guard
definition: Used when you hear news you knew nothing about, or when you pretend not to know.
examples: Quando mi hanno parlato del problema, sono caduto dalle nuvole.
examples_en: When they told me about the problem, I was completely taken by surprise.

back: to get by, to manage
definition: Used for coping with a situation or doing reasonably well at something.
literal: to pull oneself out of it
examples: Con l'inglese me la cavo abbastanza bene.
examples_en: I get by pretty well in English.

back: what can you do?
definition: Said with resignation about something that cannot be changed.
literal: what do you want to do about it
examples: Piove ancora, ma che ci vuoi fare?
examples_en: It's raining again, but what can you do?

back: how should I know, I have no idea
definition: A casual reply showing you have no idea, or a filler when searching for an example.
literal: what do I know about it
examples: Che ne so, forse è già uscito di casa.
examples_en: How should I know, maybe he's already left the house.

back: seek and you shall find
definition: Said to encourage effort, or to note that someone who looks for trouble will get it.
examples: Continua a mandare curriculum: chi cerca trova.
examples_en: Keep sending out résumés: seek and you shall find.

back: you snooze, you lose; the early bird catches the worm
definition: A proverb saying that those who are lazy or slow miss out on opportunities.
examples: Alzati presto e manda il curriculum: chi dorme non piglia pesci.
examples_en: Get up early and send your résumé: the early bird catches the worm.

back: perseverance pays off
definition: Encourages persistence, since whoever holds out longest eventually succeeds.
examples: Non mollare, chi la dura la vince!
examples_en: Don't give up, perseverance pays off!

back: if you're content with what you have, you're happy
definition: Said to suggest that those who don't demand too much are happier, often to accept a modest outcome.
examples: Non è una casa grande, ma chi si accontenta gode.
examples_en: It's not a big house, but if you're content with what you have, you're happy.

back: to turn a blind eye
definition: Means overlooking a mistake or small violation out of leniency.
examples: Per questa volta chiudo un occhio.
examples_en: I'll turn a blind eye this time.

back: I bet, I'd bet money on it
definition: Said when you are quite sure about a guess or prediction.
examples: Ci scommetto che arriva in ritardo anche oggi.
examples_en: I bet he's late again today.

back: I'm in, count me in
definition: An informal way to accept a plan or proposal.
examples: Pizza stasera? Ci sto!
examples_en: Pizza tonight? I'm in!

back: to cost an arm and a leg
definition: Used when something is extremely expensive.
literal: to cost an eye of the head
examples: Quella borsa costa un occhio della testa.
examples_en: That bag costs an arm and a leg.

back: to agree that someone is right
definition: Used when you admit that someone else's opinion is correct.
examples: Alla fine ho dovuto dare ragione a mia sorella.
examples_en: In the end I had to admit my sister was right.

back: besides, after all
definition: Adds a supporting reason that backs up what you just said.
examples: Del resto, lo sapevamo già tutti.
examples_en: After all, we all knew it already.

back: between you and me
definition: Used before sharing a confidential or frank opinion.
examples: Detto fra noi, quel film mi è sembrato noioso.
examples_en: Between you and me, that movie seemed boring.

back: every now and then
definition: Describes something that happens occasionally, at irregular intervals.
literal: from so much to so much
examples: Di tanto in tanto andiamo a mangiare fuori.
examples_en: Every now and then we go out to eat.

back: to sleep like a log
definition: Used for sleeping very deeply and for a long time.
examples: Dopo la gita ho dormito come un ghiro.
examples_en: After the trip I slept like a log.

back: to be on cloud nine
definition: Used when someone is extremely happy.
literal: to be in the seventh heaven
examples: Con la promozione è al settimo cielo.
examples_en: He's on cloud nine with the promotion.

back: to be broke
definition: Used when you have no money left.
examples: Questo mese sono al verde, non posso uscire.
examples_en: I'm broke this month, so I can't go out.

back: to keep one's word
definition: Said of a reliable person who does what they promise.
examples: Se lo ha promesso, lo farà: Paolo è di parola.
examples_en: If he promised, he'll do it: Paolo keeps his word.

back: to be sly as a fox
definition: Describes a very shrewd and cunning person.
literal: to be clever like a fox
examples: Il nostro vicino è furbo come una volpe.
examples_en: Our neighbor is sly as a fox.

back: to be capable, to be a good sort
definition: Describes someone competent, smart and reliable.
examples: Marco è un ragazzo in gamba, puoi fidarti.
examples_en: Marco is a capable guy, you can trust him.

back: to be swamped with work
definition: Used when you have far more work than you can handle.
examples: Scusa il ritardo, sono sommerso di lavoro.
examples_en: Sorry for the delay, I'm swamped with work.

back: to be a sweetheart, to be kindhearted
definition: Describes a person who is very good, gentle and generous, often despite a tough appearance.
literal: to be a piece of bread
examples: Non aver paura del nonno, è un pezzo di pane.
examples_en: Don't be afraid of Grandpa, he's a sweetheart.

back: to manage, to make it
definition: Means to succeed in doing something difficult or to arrive in time.
examples: Penso che ce la farò a finire entro stasera.
examples_en: I think I'll manage to finish by tonight.

back: to do without
definition: Used when you can live or manage without something or someone.
examples: Non posso fare a meno del caffè la mattina.
examples_en: I can't do without coffee in the morning.

back: to pay attention to, to notice
definition: Used for noticing or paying attention to something, often in the negative.
examples: Non ho fatto caso a quello che dicevano.
examples_en: I didn't pay attention to what they were saying.

back: to work overtime
definition: Used for working beyond normal hours, usually paid extra.
examples: Questa settimana ho fatto tanti straordinari.
examples_en: This week I worked a lot of overtime.

back: to act smart, to try to pull a fast one
definition: Used when someone tries to take advantage of a situation or skip the rules.
examples: Non fare il furbo, anche tu devi aspettare in fila.
examples_en: Don't try to pull a fast one, you have to wait in line too.

back: to make it in time, to be in time (to)
definition: Used when you manage to do something before it's too late; usually followed by a + infinitive.
examples: Se corri, fai ancora in tempo a prendere il treno.
examples_en: If you run, you can still catch the train.

back: to mop up the sauce with a piece of bread
definition: Used when you wipe the leftover sauce on your plate with bread, a beloved habit in Italy.
examples: Il sugo era così buono che ho fatto la scarpetta.
examples_en: The sauce was so good that I mopped it up with bread.

back: to back up, to reverse; to back out
definition: Used for driving in reverse, and figuratively for backing out of a decision.
examples: La strada era chiusa, così abbiamo fatto marcia indietro.
examples_en: The road was closed, so we reversed and went back.

back: to make a fool of oneself, to embarrass oneself
definition: Used when you do something that makes you look bad in public.
examples: Ho fatto una figuraccia davanti a tutti i colleghi.
examples_en: I embarrassed myself in front of all my colleagues.

back: to get in touch, to show up
definition: Used when someone contacts you or appears after a long silence, or as a reproach if they don't.
examples: Non ti fai vivo da mesi: tutto bene?
examples_en: I haven't heard from you in months. Is everything OK?

back: when all is said and done, after all
definition: Introduces a conclusion or the essential point after weighing everything.
literal: at the end of the accounts
examples: In fin dei conti, non è andata poi così male.
examples_en: When all is said and done, it didn't go that badly.

back: in short, in a nutshell
definition: Used to sum something up briefly.
examples: In poche parole, non abbiamo abbastanza soldi.
examples_en: In a nutshell, we don't have enough money.

back: in the blink of an eye
definition: Describes something done or happening extremely fast.
literal: in a beat of the eye
examples: Ha finito i compiti in un batter d'occhio.
examples_en: He finished his homework in the blink of an eye.

front: l'erba del vicino è sempre più verde
lemma: l'erba del vicino è sempre più verde
back: the grass is always greener on the other side
definition: Said about people who envy others and think they have it better.
literal: the neighbor's grass is always greener
examples: Invidi la sua vita, ma l'erba del vicino è sempre più verde.
examples_en: You envy his life, but the grass is always greener on the other side.

back: the icing on the cake, the cherry on top
definition: Describes the final pleasant touch that makes something perfect.
literal: the little cherry on the cake
examples: Il bel tempo è stato la ciliegina sulla torta.
examples_en: The nice weather was the icing on the cake.

back: to give it one's all
definition: Used when someone makes the maximum effort to reach a goal.
literal: to put it all in it
examples: Ce l'ho messa tutta, ma non è bastato.
examples_en: I gave it my all, but it wasn't enough.

back: to set off, to hit the road
definition: Used when starting a trip, especially a longer one.
examples: Ci siamo messi in viaggio alle cinque del mattino.
examples_en: We hit the road at five in the morning.

back: to start dating, to become a couple
definition: Used when two people begin a romantic relationship.
examples: Marco e Giulia si sono messi insieme a settembre.
examples_en: Marco and Giulia got together in September.

back: when in doubt, just in case
definition: Introduces the safe choice you make because you are unsure.
examples: Nel dubbio, porta un ombrello.
examples_en: When in doubt, bring an umbrella.

back: no way, not in a million years
definition: A strong refusal or denial; 'neanche per sogno' is equivalent.
examples: Prestargli la macchina? Nemmeno per sogno!
examples_en: Lend him my car? Not in a million years!

back: it has nothing to do with it, that's beside the point
definition: Used to say that something is irrelevant to the topic or has no connection to the matter at hand. It comes from 'entrarci' (to have to do with something).
examples: Questo non c'entra con quello che stiamo dicendo.
examples_en: That has nothing to do with what we're talking about.

back: things come in threes
definition: Said when something has happened twice and people expect it to happen a third time.
literal: there is no two without three
examples: Hai già bucato due volte? Non c'è due senza tre!
examples_en: You've already had two flat tires? Things come in threes!

back: not necessarily, that's not a given
definition: Used to cast doubt on an assumption or generalization; usually followed by 'che' + subjunctive.
examples: Non è detto che il treno sia in orario.
examples_en: The train isn't necessarily going to be on time.

front: paese che vai, usanza che trovi
lemma: paese che vai, usanza che trovi
back: when in Rome, do as the Romans do
definition: Said about customs that differ from place to place and the need to adapt to them.
literal: country you go to, custom you find
examples: Qui si cena tardissimo, ma paese che vai, usanza che trovi.
examples_en: People eat dinner really late here, but when in Rome, do as the Romans do.

back: of course, no wonder / necessarily
definition: Said when something is only natural, or when someone has no choice.
examples: Per forza ha vinto, si allena ogni giorno!
examples_en: Of course he won, he trains every day!

back: to lose touch with, to lose sight of
definition: Used when you no longer see or hear from someone you used to be close to.
examples: Dopo il liceo ci siamo persi di vista.
examples_en: After high school we lost touch.

back: to lose one's patience
definition: Used when someone finally gets angry or irritated after holding back.
examples: Alla fine ho perso la pazienza e ho urlato.
examples_en: In the end I lost my patience and yelled.

back: to complete, to see through
definition: Used for finishing a task, project or commitment, often despite obstacles.
examples: Siamo riusciti a portare a termine il lavoro in tempo.
examples_en: We managed to complete the job on time.

front: prendere due piccioni con una fava
lemma: prendere due piccioni con una fava
back: to kill two birds with one stone
definition: Used when a single action achieves two goals.
literal: to catch two pigeons with one bean
examples: Vado in banca e passo in posta: due piccioni con una fava.
examples_en: I'll go to the bank and stop by the post office: two birds with one stone.

back: to take offense, to get upset
definition: Used when someone reacts badly to something said or done.
examples: Non te la prendere, scherzavo!
examples_en: Don't take it personally, I was joking!

front: quando il gatto non c'è i topi ballano
lemma: quando il gatto non c'è i topi ballano
back: when the cat's away the mice will play
definition: Said when people misbehave or relax once the boss or authority is absent.
literal: when the cat isn't there the mice dance
examples: Il capo è in ferie e in ufficio nessuno lavora: quando il gatto non c'è, i topi ballano.
examples_en: The boss is on vacation and nobody's working: when the cat's away, the mice will play.

back: to break down
definition: Used when a car or vehicle stops working on the road.
examples: Siamo rimasti in panne sull'autostrada per due ore.
examples_en: We broke down on the highway and were stuck for two hours.

back: he who laughs last laughs best
definition: Used to say that final success matters more than early advantages, often as a mild warning.
literal: he laughs well who laughs last
examples: Per ora vincono loro, ma ride bene chi ride ultimo.
examples_en: For now they're winning, but he who laughs last laughs best.

back: to roll up one's sleeves
definition: Used when someone gets ready to tackle a hard task or a difficult situation with determination.
examples: Dopo l'alluvione, tutti si sono rimboccati le maniche.
examples_en: After the flood, everyone rolled up their sleeves.

front: rosso di sera bel tempo si spera
lemma: rosso di sera bel tempo si spera
back: red sky at night, sailor's delight
definition: A weather saying: a red sunset suggests that the next day will be fair.
literal: red in the evening, one hopes for good weather
examples: Che tramonto! Rosso di sera bel tempo si spera.
examples_en: What a sunset! Red sky at night, sailor's delight.

back: say hi to your mother for me
definition: A friendly way to send regards to someone's relative, adaptable to anyone (e.g. 'salutami tuo fratello').
examples: Salutami tua madre quando la senti!
examples_en: Say hi to your mom for me when you talk to her!

back: to stop it, to quit it
definition: Used to tell someone to stop doing something annoying; usually as an imperative ('smettila!').
examples: Smettila di fare rumore, sto studiando!
examples_en: Stop making noise, I'm studying!

back: take care
definition: An affectionate, informal goodbye among friends or family.
examples: Ci sentiamo presto, stammi bene!
examples_en: Talk soon, take care!

front: stare con le mani in mano
lemma: stare con le mani in mano
back: to sit idle, to twiddle one's thumbs
definition: Used to criticize or describe someone who does nothing when there is work to do.
literal: to stay with hands in hand
examples: Non puoi stare con le mani in mano mentre noi lavoriamo.
examples_en: You can't just sit idle while we work.

back: like father, like son
definition: A proverb used when a child shows the same traits or habits as a parent.
examples: Anche lui è testardo: tale padre, tale figlio!
examples_en: He's stubborn too: like father, like son!

back: just for a change, as usual (ironic)
definition: Said ironically when something negative happens yet again.
examples: Tanto per cambiare, il treno è in ritardo.
examples_en: Big surprise, the train is late again.

back: to get by, to keep going
definition: Used to say you are managing to continue despite difficulties, often with money or work.
examples: Con questo stipendio si tira avanti, ma niente di più.
examples_en: With this salary we get by, but nothing more.

front: tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare
lemma: tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare
back: easier said than done
definition: Used when promises or plans are far easier to state than to carry out.
literal: between saying and doing there is the sea
examples: Dici di voler smettere di fumare, ma tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.
examples_en: You say you want to quit smoking, but it's easier said than done.

back: besides, by the way, what's more
definition: Adds an extra point or detail to an argument or story.
examples: Non ho voglia di uscire, e tra l'altro piove.
examples_en: I don't feel like going out, and besides, it's raining.

back: all of a sudden
definition: Introduces a sudden event in a story.
examples: Tutt'a un tratto si è spenta la luce.
examples_en: All of a sudden the light went out.

back: every little bit helps
definition: Used to say that even a small or imperfect contribution is useful.
examples: Anche cinque euro vanno bene: tutto fa brodo.
examples_en: Even five euros is fine: every little bit helps.

back: cheap, at a low price
definition: Describes something inexpensive, often with a hint of good value.
examples: Ho comprato questa giacca a buon mercato.
examples_en: I bought this jacket cheap.

front: a caval donato non si guarda in bocca
lemma: a caval donato non si guarda in bocca
back: don't look a gift horse in the mouth
definition: Advises not to criticize a gift or a favor you've received.
literal: you don't look in the mouth of a donated horse
examples: Magari è vecchio, ma a caval donato non si guarda in bocca.
examples_en: Maybe it's old, but don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

back: to say the least
definition: Used to stress that the word you chose is an understatement.
examples: Il film è stato a dir poco noioso.
examples_en: The movie was boring, to say the least.

back: in the long run
definition: Used to say what will happen or become clear after a long period.
examples: A lungo andare questo lavoro mi stancherà.
examples_en: In the long run this job will wear me out.

back: desperate times call for desperate measures
definition: Used to justify drastic action when a situation is very serious.
examples: Vendo la macchina: a mali estremi, estremi rimedi.
examples_en: I'm selling the car: desperate times call for desperate measures.

back: in my view
definition: A slightly more formal alternative to 'secondo me', common in discussions and at work.
examples: A mio avviso, il progetto va rivisto.
examples_en: In my view, the project needs to be reviewed.

back: perfectly, expertly, by the book
definition: Used to say a job was done with professional skill and care.
examples: L'idraulico ha sistemato tutto a regola d'arte.
examples_en: The plumber fixed everything perfectly.

back: on the fly, quickly, right away
definition: Used for doing something quickly or catching an opportunity immediately.
examples: Ho preso il treno al volo.
examples_en: I caught the train just in time.

back: to fall through, to be ruined
definition: Used when a plan or deal fails or is cancelled.
examples: Per la pioggia la gita è andata a monte.
examples_en: Because of the rain, the trip fell through.

back: to go down the wrong way; to be hard to stomach
definition: Literally for food going down the wrong pipe, figuratively for something you can't stand or that goes wrong.
examples: Mi è andato di traverso il boccone e ho tossito.
examples_en: The bite went down the wrong way and I coughed.

back: to have one's heart in one's mouth
definition: Used when feeling intense fear, anxiety or suspense.
literal: to have the heart in the throat
examples: Avevo il cuore in gola mentre aspettavo i risultati.
examples_en: My heart was in my mouth while I waited for the results.

back: to be in dire straits, to be under great pressure
definition: Used when you are in serious difficulty, especially financial or with a deadline. 'Essere con l'acqua alla gola' is a less common variant.
literal: to have water up to the throat
examples: Con tutti questi debiti abbiamo l'acqua alla gola.
examples_en: With all these debts we're in deep trouble.

back: to be a blabbermouth, to be unable to keep a secret
definition: Describes someone who can't keep secrets or says too much, or who is sharp-tongued.
examples: Non dirle niente, ha la lingua lunga.
examples_en: Don't tell her anything, she can't keep her mouth shut.

back: to be in a bad mood, to have gotten up on the wrong side of the bed
definition: Said of someone who is grumpy for no clear reason.
examples: Stamattina ha la luna storta, meglio non parlargli.
examples_en: He's in a bad mood this morning; better not talk to him.

back: to have one's hands tied
definition: Used when you cannot act freely because of rules or circumstances.
examples: Mi dispiace, ma ho le mani legate.
examples_en: I'm sorry, but my hands are tied.

back: to have a soft spot for
definition: Used for a special fondness or attraction toward a person or thing.
examples: La nonna ha un debole per il nipote più piccolo.
examples_en: Grandma has a soft spot for her youngest grandson.

back: to have a lump in one's throat
definition: Describes being choked up with emotion, usually sadness.
literal: to have a knot in the throat
examples: Ho un nodo alla gola ogni volta che la saluto.
examples_en: I get a lump in my throat every time I say goodbye to her.

back: to have a lot of nerve
definition: Used for someone who acts shamelessly bold or cheeky.
literal: to have a nice tough face
examples: Hai una bella faccia tosta a chiedermi altri soldi!
examples_en: You've got some nerve asking me for more money!

back: a barking dog doesn't bite; his bark is worse than his bite
definition: Said of people who make loud threats but are not really dangerous.
literal: a dog that barks doesn't bite
examples: Non preoccuparti del capo: can che abbaia non morde.
examples_en: Don't worry about the boss: his bark is worse than his bite.

front: cercare un ago in un pagliaio
lemma: cercare un ago in un pagliaio
back: to look for a needle in a haystack
definition: Used for a nearly impossible search or task.
literal: to look for a needle in a haystack
examples: Trovare le chiavi in questo caos è come cercare un ago in un pagliaio.
examples_en: Finding the keys in this mess is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

front: chi fa da sé fa per tre
lemma: chi fa da sé fa per tre
back: if you want something done right, do it yourself
definition: A proverb saying that doing a task yourself is more efficient than relying on others.
literal: who does for himself does for three
examples: Faccio io, chi fa da sé fa per tre.
examples_en: I'll do it; if you want it done right, do it yourself.

back: sow the wind, reap the whirlwind
definition: Warns that bad or reckless actions bring even worse consequences.
examples: Ha trattato tutti male e ora è solo: chi semina vento raccoglie tempesta.
examples_en: He treated everyone badly and now he's alone: sow the wind, reap the whirlwind.

back: to stand someone up, to bail
definition: Used when someone fails to show up to a meeting or cancels at the last minute without warning.
examples: Mi ha dato buca all'ultimo momento, senza nemmeno avvisare.
examples_en: He stood me up at the last minute, without even letting me know.

back: to take for granted, to assume
definition: Used when you assume something is certain without checking it.
examples: Non dare per scontato che ti aiuteranno.
examples_en: Don't take it for granted that they'll help you.

back: to put on airs
definition: Describes someone who acts superior or important.
examples: Da quando ha la nuova macchina si dà delle arie.
examples_en: Since he got the new car he's been putting on airs.

back: to shoot oneself in the foot
definition: Used when someone harms themselves through their own actions.
literal: to hit one's own feet with a hoe
examples: Litigando con il cliente ti sei dato la zappa sui piedi.
examples_en: By arguing with the client you shot yourself in the foot.

back: all of a sudden, out of the blue
definition: Used for something that happens abruptly and unexpectedly.
examples: Di punto in bianco ha deciso di partire.
examples_en: Out of the blue, he decided to leave.

back: to give one's own opinion, to have one's say
definition: Used when someone speaks up and shares their personal view on a matter. The variant 'dire la sua' is also common.
examples: Alla riunione ognuno ha potuto dire la propria.
examples_en: At the meeting everyone was able to have their say.

back: to be easygoing and approachable
definition: Describes a friendly, unpretentious person who is easy to talk to.
examples: Il nuovo professore è simpatico e molto alla mano.
examples_en: The new professor is nice and very approachable.

back: to be as good as gold, to be very kind
definition: Describes a very kind, gentle person with a good heart.
examples: Mio nonno era buono come il pane.
examples_en: My grandfather was as good as gold.

back: to be beside oneself
definition: Describes being overwhelmed by anger, joy or distress.
examples: Era fuori di sé dalla rabbia.
examples_en: He was beside himself with rage.

back: to be out of the way
definition: Used for a place that is remote or inconvenient to reach.
literal: to be outside the hand (out of reach)
examples: L'hotel è carino ma un po' fuori mano.
examples_en: The hotel is nice but a bit out of the way.

back: to be stuck in traffic
definition: Used to describe being caught in a heavy traffic jam.
literal: to be bottled up in the traffic
examples: Scusa il ritardo, sono imbottigliato nel traffico.
examples_en: Sorry I'm late, I'm stuck in traffic.

front: essere la goccia che fa traboccare il vaso
lemma: essere la goccia che fa traboccare il vaso
back: to be the last straw
definition: Used for a small thing that finally makes a bad situation unbearable.
literal: to be the drop that makes the vase overflow
examples: Quel ritardo è stato la goccia che ha fatto traboccare il vaso.
examples_en: That delay was the last straw.

back: to be the black sheep
definition: Used for the family member who is seen as the disgrace or who differs from the rest.
examples: In famiglia sono sempre stato la pecora nera.
examples_en: In my family I've always been the black sheep.

back: to be pricey, steep
definition: Said of a price or bill that is higher than expected.
examples: Il conto era davvero salato.
examples_en: The bill was really steep.

back: to be wound up, to be hyper
definition: Describes someone excited and energetic, like an engine running at high rpm.
examples: I bambini sono su di giri per la festa.
examples_en: The kids are all wound up about the party.

back: to remain to be seen
definition: Said when the outcome is still uncertain and can't be judged yet.
examples: Che il piano funzioni è tutto da vedere.
examples_en: Whether the plan will work remains to be seen.

back: to be an open book
definition: Describes someone whose feelings and thoughts are easy to read.
examples: Con te sono un libro aperto, non ho segreti.
examples_en: With you I'm an open book, I have no secrets.

back: to be a tough nut to crack
definition: Describes a person who is tough, resistant or hard to convince or beat.
examples: Il nostro capo è un osso duro in trattativa.
examples_en: Our boss is a tough nut to crack in negotiations.

back: to be a hothead
definition: Describes an impulsive person who gets angry or reckless easily.
examples: Fai attenzione, tuo cugino è una testa calda.
examples_en: Be careful, your cousin is a hothead.

back: to bend over backwards, to do whatever it takes
definition: Used when someone makes extraordinary efforts to manage a difficult situation, such as balancing work and family.
examples: Faccio i salti mortali per conciliare lavoro e figli.
examples_en: I bend over backwards to balance work and kids.

back: to take a bridge day off (to get a long weekend)
definition: Said when a working day falls between a holiday and a weekend and you take it off too, making a long break.
examples: Venerdì facciamo il ponte e andiamo al mare.
examples_en: We're taking Friday off for a long weekend at the beach.

back: to offer one's condolences
definition: Used to express sympathy to someone who has lost a loved one.
examples: Sono andato a fare le condoglianze alla famiglia.
examples_en: I went to offer my condolences to the family.

back: to turn a deaf ear
definition: Used when someone pretends not to hear a request or advice they don't like.
examples: Gli ho chiesto aiuto, ma lui ha fatto orecchie da mercante.
examples_en: I asked him for help, but he turned a deaf ear.

back: to have a layover, to stop over
definition: Used for a stop at an intermediate airport or port during a trip.
literal: to make a stop at a port
examples: Il volo per New York fa scalo a Francoforte.
examples_en: The flight to New York has a layover in Frankfurt.

back: to get nowhere, to achieve nothing
definition: Used when an attempt or effort fails to produce any result.
literal: to make a hole in the water
examples: Abbiamo provato a convincerlo, ma abbiamo fatto un buco nell'acqua.
examples_en: We tried to convince him, but we got nowhere.

back: to lead a dog's life
definition: Describes a hard, miserable or exhausting way of living.
literal: to live a life of dogs
examples: Con due lavori faccio una vita da cani.
examples_en: With two jobs I lead a dog's life.

back: as if, fat chance, just imagine
definition: Used ironically to say something is very unlikely or out of the question.
examples: Lui che aiuta qualcuno? Figuriamoci!
examples_en: Him helping someone? As if!

back: to pour oil on troubled waters; to calm things down
definition: Used when someone calms down a tense or heated situation.
literal: to throw water on the fire
examples: Maria ha cercato di gettare acqua sul fuoco durante la lite.
examples_en: Maria tried to calm things down during the fight.

back: to beat around the bush
definition: Describes avoiding the real point instead of saying it directly.
examples: Smettila di girarci intorno e dimmi la verità.
examples_en: Stop beating around the bush and tell me the truth.

front: il mattino ha l'oro in bocca
lemma: il mattino ha l'oro in bocca
back: the early bird catches the worm
definition: Said to praise getting up early, since the morning hours are the most productive.
literal: the morning has gold in its mouth
examples: Alzati presto, il mattino ha l'oro in bocca.
examples_en: Get up early, the early bird catches the worm.

back: the more you have, the more you want
definition: Said when starting something awakens a desire for more, whether food, success or money.
examples: Volevo solo un assaggio, ma l'appetito vien mangiando.
examples_en: I only wanted a taste, but the more you have, the more you want.

back: to work like a dog
definition: Describes working very hard and tirelessly, often without much reward.
examples: Lavora come un mulo da mattina a sera.
examples_en: He works like a dog from morning till night.

back: to work under the table
definition: Describes working without a legal contract or paying taxes.
examples: Per anni ha lavorato in nero in un ristorante.
examples_en: For years he worked under the table at a restaurant.

back: to keep a cool head, to keep one's cool
definition: Describes staying calm in a dangerous or stressful situation. 'Avere sangue freddo' is also used for someone who naturally stays calm.
examples: Il pilota ha mantenuto il sangue freddo durante l'emergenza.
examples_en: The pilot kept a cool head during the emergency.

back: to question, to call into question
definition: Used when you challenge whether something is true or reliable.
examples: Nessuno mette in dubbio la sua onestà.
examples_en: No one questions his honesty.

back: to start a family
definition: Used for getting married and having children, or settling into family life.
examples: A trent'anni ha deciso di mettere su famiglia.
examples_en: At thirty he decided to start a family.

back: to not mince words
definition: Describes a person who says exactly what they think, however blunt.
literal: to have no hairs on the tongue
examples: Mia nonna non ha peli sulla lingua.
examples_en: My grandmother doesn't mince words.

back: there's no doubt about it
definition: Used to say that something is absolutely certain and cannot be argued.
examples: È il miglior ristorante della città, non ci piove.
examples_en: It's the best restaurant in town, no doubt about it.

back: not to know what to do, to be at a loss
definition: Used when you are confused and cannot decide how to act.
literal: not to know which fish to catch
examples: Il computer si è rotto e non so che pesci pigliare.
examples_en: The computer broke and I don't know what to do.

front: occhio non vede, cuore non duole
lemma: occhio non vede, cuore non duole
back: what the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over
definition: Said when what you don't know or see can't upset you.
literal: eye doesn't see, heart doesn't hurt
examples: Non guardare il conto: occhio non vede, cuore non duole.
examples_en: Don't look at the bill: what the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over.

back: to split the bill evenly
definition: Used when everyone pays an equal share of the bill, regardless of what they ate.
examples: Siamo in sei, paghiamo alla romana?
examples_en: There are six of us, shall we split the bill evenly?

back: to talk nonsense, to talk off the top of one's head
definition: Said of someone who talks without knowing or thinking about what they say.
examples: Non ascoltarlo, parla a vanvera.
examples_en: Don't listen to him, he's talking nonsense.

back: so to speak, as it were
definition: Signals that a word or description is not meant to be exact.
examples: È un esperto di vini, per così dire.
examples_en: He's an expert on wines, so to speak.

back: it never rains but it pours
definition: Said when misfortune (or sometimes good fortune) keeps falling on those who already have plenty of it.
examples: Ha perso il lavoro e ora gli si è rotta la macchina: piove sul bagnato.
examples_en: He lost his job and now his car has broken down: it never rains but it pours.

back: to stand up for, to take the side of
definition: Used when you defend someone who is being criticized or attacked.
examples: Mio padre ha preso le difese di mio fratello.
examples_en: My father stood up for my brother.

back: to make a silly mistake, to get the wrong end of the stick
definition: Used when you make a mistake because you misunderstood or misjudged something.
examples: Ho preso un granchio: la riunione era ieri, non oggi.
examples_en: I made a blunder: the meeting was yesterday, not today.

back: to make a blunder, to get it badly wrong
definition: Used when you make a bad mistake, especially a wrong judgment about something or someone.
examples: Ho preso una cantonata: pensavo fosse più gentile.
examples_en: I got it totally wrong: I thought he was nicer.

back: to be stunned; to be dumbfounded
definition: Describes being so shocked that you cannot react.
examples: Quando l'ho saputo, sono rimasto di sasso.
examples_en: When I heard, I was dumbfounded.

back: barring any surprises, unless something comes up
definition: Used when making a plan that is likely but not guaranteed.
examples: Salvo imprevisti, arriviamo per le otto.
examples_en: Barring any surprises, we'll arrive by eight.

back: for that matter, as for that
definition: Adds a related point, often expanding on or turning around what someone just said.
examples: Se è per questo, nemmeno io ho mai visto quel film.
examples_en: For that matter, I've never seen that movie either.

back: to feel like a fish out of water
definition: Describes feeling awkward or out of place in an unfamiliar environment.
literal: to feel like a fish out of water
examples: Alla festa mi sentivo un pesce fuor d'acqua.
examples_en: At the party I felt like a fish out of water.

back: beyond the shadow of a doubt
definition: A stronger, emphatic version of 'senza dubbio'.
examples: Era lui, senza ombra di dubbio.
examples_en: It was him, beyond the shadow of a doubt.

back: to break one's back
definition: Used for doing very tiring physical or hard work, often with a complaint.
examples: Mi spacco la schiena e nessuno lo apprezza.
examples_en: I break my back and nobody appreciates it.

back: to spit it out; to come clean
definition: Used to urge someone to finally say what they have been holding back.
examples: Dai, sputa il rospo: cosa è successo?
examples_en: Come on, spit it out: what happened?

back: to unplug, to switch off and take a break
definition: Used when you stop working or worrying to rest and relax.
examples: Questo weekend voglio staccare la spina e non pensare al lavoro.
examples_en: This weekend I want to unplug and not think about work.

back: to be anxious, to be worried sick
definition: Common colloquial way to say you're anxious while waiting for something.
examples: Sto con l'ansia da stamattina per il colloquio.
examples_en: I've been anxious since this morning about the interview.

back: to be on pins and needles
definition: Used when anxiously waiting for news or an outcome.
examples: Siamo sulle spine in attesa dell'esito.
examples_en: We're on pins and needles waiting for the outcome.

back: along the way, on the way
definition: Used for something that happens or is decided during a trip or while a process unfolds.
examples: Strada facendo ti racconto tutto.
examples_en: I'll tell you everything on the way.

back: to cut it short, to get to the point
definition: Used when you stop a long discussion or explanation and go straight to the point.
examples: Per tagliare corto, non ci vado.
examples_en: To cut it short, I'm not going.

back: to care about, to be keen on
definition: Used when something or someone matters a lot to you; followed by 'a'.
examples: Ci tengo molto a questo lavoro.
examples_en: I care a lot about this job.

back: to sulk, to give someone the cold shoulder
definition: Used when someone stays upset and silent after an argument or disappointment.
examples: Mia sorella mi tiene il broncio da due giorni.
examples_en: My sister has been sulking and giving me the cold shoulder for two days.

back: to hit rock bottom
definition: Used when someone reaches the worst point of a bad period.
examples: Dopo il divorzio ha toccato il fondo.
examples_en: After the divorce he hit rock bottom.

front: tutte le strade portano a Roma
lemma: tutte le strade portano a Roma
back: all roads lead to Rome
definition: A proverb meaning there are many ways to reach the same goal.
examples: Non importa quale strada prendi: tutte le strade portano a Roma.
examples_en: It doesn't matter which road you take: all roads lead to Rome.

back: at a rock-bottom price
definition: Describes a very low, heavily discounted price. It is almost always used in this form.
examples: Ho trovato un divano a prezzo stracciato.
examples_en: I found a couch at a rock-bottom price.

back: a stone's throw away
definition: Used to say something is very close by.
examples: Il mare è a un tiro di schioppo da casa nostra.
examples_en: The sea is a stone's throw from our house.

back: best friends, thick as thieves
definition: Describes very close friends who stick together through everything.
examples: Siamo amici per la pelle dai tempi delle elementari.
examples_en: We've been best friends since elementary school.

back: to go downhill, to fall apart
definition: Used when a situation, business or plan deteriorates badly.
examples: Dopo la crisi, l'azienda è andata a rotoli.
examples_en: After the crisis, the company went downhill.

back: to hit the roof, to fly into a rage
definition: Used for suddenly becoming furious.
examples: Mio fratello è andato in bestia quando ha visto il graffio.
examples_en: My brother hit the roof when he saw the scratch.

front: avere i nervi a fior di pelle
lemma: avere i nervi a fior di pelle
back: to be on edge
definition: Describes someone who is very tense and easily irritated.
literal: to have nerves at the skin's surface
examples: Oggi ho i nervi a fior di pelle per l'esame.
examples_en: Today I'm on edge because of the exam.

back: to be stingy
definition: Said of someone who is reluctant to spend money or pay for others.
literal: to have a short little arm
examples: Con le mance ha sempre il braccino corto.
examples_en: He's always stingy when it comes to tips.

back: to hold a grudge
definition: Used when someone harbors resentment against another person.
examples: Ha ancora il dente avvelenato con il suo ex socio.
examples_en: He still holds a grudge against his former partner.

back: to have a finger in the pie
definition: Said of someone who is involved in or has influence over a business or affair.
literal: to have one's hands in the dough
examples: Quel politico ha le mani in pasta in ogni settore.
examples_en: That politician has a finger in every pie.

back: to have common sense
definition: Describes someone who is sensible and wise; often used negatively for those who aren't.
literal: to have salt in one's pumpkin
examples: Se avessi un po' di sale in zucca non lo faresti.
examples_en: If you had a little common sense you wouldn't do it.

back: to be hopping mad
definition: Describes someone extremely angry or in a terrible mood.
literal: to have a devil for every hair
examples: Oggi il capo ha un diavolo per capello.
examples_en: Today the boss is hopping mad.

back: to have a tough problem to deal with
definition: Used when you face an annoying, difficult task or problem that must be handled.
literal: to have a cat to skin
examples: Con questo contratto abbiamo una bella gatta da pelare.
examples_en: With this contract we have a real headache on our hands.

back: to slack off, to lounge around
definition: Describes working slowly or lazily, doing the bare minimum.
examples: Il lunedì in ufficio battono tutti la fiacca.
examples_en: On Mondays everyone in the office slacks off.

back: to nitpick, to split hairs
definition: Used for someone who searches for tiny flaws in everything.
literal: to look for the hair in the egg
examples: Il mio capo cerca sempre il pelo nell'uovo.
examples_en: My boss always nitpicks.

back: in all likelihood, most probably
definition: Used to say something is very likely, in a slightly formal tone.
examples: Con ogni probabilità la riunione sarà rinviata.
examples_en: In all likelihood the meeting will be postponed.

front: dire pane al pane e vino al vino
lemma: dire pane al pane e vino al vino
back: to call a spade a spade
definition: Used for speaking frankly and directly, without softening the truth.
literal: to say bread to bread and wine to wine
examples: Io dico pane al pane e vino al vino, sai come sono fatto.
examples_en: I call a spade a spade, you know what I'm like.

back: to be at the end of one's rope, to be worn out or nearly finished
definition: Fruit comes at the end of an Italian meal, so it means being near the end of one's resources or strength.
examples: Con questo lavoro sono proprio alla frutta.
examples_en: With this job I'm completely worn out.

back: to be head over heels for
definition: Used for being very much in love or infatuated with someone.
examples: Luca è cotto di lei, ma non glielo dice.
examples_en: Luca is head over heels for her, but he doesn't tell her.

back: to be open-minded
definition: Describes a person who is tolerant and open to different ideas.
examples: I miei genitori sono di larghe vedute.
examples_en: My parents are open-minded.

back: to be lenient
definition: Said of someone who is easygoing or generous with rules, grades or money.
examples: La professoressa di storia è di manica larga con i voti.
examples_en: The history teacher is lenient with grades.

back: to be far from finished, to be nowhere near done
definition: Used when a project or negotiation is still far from being completed.
literal: to be on the high sea
examples: Il progetto è ancora in alto mare.
examples_en: The project is still nowhere near done.

front: essere tra l'incudine e il martello
lemma: essere tra l'incudine e il martello
back: to be between a rock and a hard place
definition: Used when you are stuck between two equally unpleasant options.
literal: to be between the anvil and the hammer
examples: Sono tra l'incudine e il martello: qualunque scelta farò, sarà sbagliata.
examples_en: I'm between a rock and a hard place: whatever I choose will be wrong.

front: essere un lupo travestito da agnello
lemma: essere un lupo travestito da agnello
back: to be a wolf in sheep's clothing
definition: Describes someone who looks harmless or kind but is actually dangerous.
literal: to be a wolf disguised as a lamb
examples: Sembra gentile, ma è un lupo travestito da agnello.
examples_en: He seems kind, but he's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

back: to be a hearty eater, to enjoy good food
definition: Describes someone who eats with great appetite and enjoyment.
examples: Mio zio è una buona forchetta, preparati a cucinare tanto.
examples_en: My uncle is a hearty eater, so get ready to cook a lot.

back: to make the numbers add up, to balance the budget
definition: Used for managing a budget so that income covers expenses.
examples: Con due figli è difficile far quadrare i conti.
examples_en: With two kids it's hard to make the numbers add up.

back: to make a killing, to do a roaring business
definition: Used when a person or business earns a lot of money.
examples: Il bar vicino alla stazione fa affari d'oro.
examples_en: The café near the station is doing a roaring business.

back: to flirt with someone, to hit on someone
definition: Used when someone is trying to court or charm another person.
literal: to make the thread to someone
examples: Il tuo collega fa il filo a Sara da settimane.
examples_en: Your colleague has been hitting on Sara for weeks.

back: to pay one's dues, to work one's way up from the bottom
definition: Describes starting in a humble, low-paid position to learn a job and advance.
examples: Ha fatto la gavetta prima di diventare direttore.
examples_en: He paid his dues before becoming director.

front: il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio
lemma: il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio
back: a leopard can't change its spots
definition: Said when someone doesn't change their bad habits despite appearances.
literal: the wolf loses its fur but not its vice
examples: Ha promesso di smettere, ma si sa: il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio.
examples_en: He promised to quit, but you know how it is: a leopard can't change its spots.

front: in men che non si dica
lemma: in men che non si dica
back: in no time at all
definition: Describes something done so quickly it hardly takes time to say it.
examples: Ha mangiato tutto in men che non si dica.
examples_en: He ate everything in no time at all.

back: to keep things running, to keep the show going
definition: Used when someone keeps a business, family or organization functioning, often with limited means.
examples: Da anni è lei che manda avanti la baracca.
examples_en: For years she has been the one keeping things running.

back: to catch on, to figure out what's going on
definition: Used when someone realizes a hidden trick or intention.
examples: Ha mangiato la foglia e non ha firmato.
examples_en: He caught on and didn't sign.

front: meglio un uovo oggi che una gallina domani
lemma: meglio un uovo oggi che una gallina domani
back: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
definition: A proverb advising you to take a sure, smaller gain over a bigger uncertain one.
literal: better an egg today than a hen tomorrow
examples: Prendo l'offerta: meglio un uovo oggi che una gallina domani.
examples_en: I'll take the offer: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

back: to beat around the bush
definition: Used when someone avoids getting to the point and drags things out.
literal: to lead the dog around the threshing floor
examples: Smettila di menare il can per l'aia e dimmi la verità.
examples_en: Stop beating around the bush and tell me the truth.

back: to stake one's life on it, to vouch for something
definition: Used to say you are absolutely certain, usually about someone's honesty.
literal: to put one's hand in the fire for it
examples: Su di lei ci metto la mano sul fuoco.
examples_en: I'd stake my life on her.

front: mettere i bastoni tra le ruote
lemma: mettere i bastoni tra le ruote
back: to throw a wrench in the works, to put obstacles in someone's way
definition: Used when someone deliberately obstructs another person's plans.
literal: to put sticks between the wheels
examples: Invece di aiutarmi, mi mette sempre i bastoni tra le ruote.
examples_en: Instead of helping me, he's always putting obstacles in my way.

front: mettere il carro davanti ai buoi
lemma: mettere il carro davanti ai buoi
back: to put the cart before the horse
definition: Used when someone does things in the wrong order or rushes ahead.
literal: to put the cart before the oxen
examples: Comprare i mobili prima della casa è mettere il carro davanti ai buoi.
examples_en: Buying furniture before the house is putting the cart before the horse.

back: to touch a sore spot; to touch a nerve
definition: Used when someone touches on a painful subject.
literal: to put the finger in the wound
examples: Hai messo il dito nella piaga parlando del suo divorzio.
examples_en: You touched a sore spot by mentioning his divorce.

back: to bite off more than one can chew
definition: Said when someone takes on too many tasks or projects at once.
literal: to put too much meat on the fire
examples: Hai messo troppa carne al fuoco, non finirai mai.
examples_en: You've taken on too much, you'll never finish.

front: non avere né capo né coda
lemma: non avere né capo né coda
back: to make no sense at all
definition: Describes a story, speech or idea that is confused and incoherent.
literal: to have neither head nor tail
examples: Il tuo discorso non ha né capo né coda.
examples_en: What you're saying makes no sense at all.

back: to spare no expense
definition: Used when someone spends freely without worrying about cost.
literal: not to pay attention to expenses
examples: Per il matrimonio non hanno badato a spese.
examples_en: For the wedding they spared no expense.

front: non essere pane per i propri denti
lemma: non essere pane per i propri denti
back: to be too tough for someone, to be out of one's league
definition: Said about a task or person too difficult or demanding for you to handle.
literal: to not be bread for one's teeth
examples: Questo esame non è pane per i miei denti.
examples_en: This exam is too tough for me.

back: to be no genius
definition: A mild, ironic way to say someone isn't very bright.
examples: Luca è simpatico, ma non è un'aquila.
examples_en: Luca is nice, but he's no genius.

back: it's flawless, it holds up perfectly
definition: Said of an argument or reasoning that is perfectly logical, with no flaws.
examples: Il tuo ragionamento non fa una piega.
examples_en: Your reasoning is airtight.

front: non vendere la pelle dell'orso prima di averlo ucciso
lemma: non vendere la pelle dell'orso prima di averlo ucciso
back: don't count your chickens before they hatch
definition: Advises against counting on a result before it is certain.
literal: don't sell the bear's skin before killing it
examples: Non è ancora tuo: non vendere la pelle dell'orso prima di averlo ucciso.
examples_en: It's not yours yet: don't count your chickens before they hatch.

back: by the skin of one's teeth
definition: Used when you barely succeed or escape a bad outcome.
literal: by the tear of the bonnet
examples: Ho passato l'esame per il rotto della cuffia.
examples_en: I passed the exam by the skin of my teeth.

back: to shed crocodile tears
definition: Used for insincere grief or remorse shown for appearances.
examples: Dopo averlo licenziato, ora piange lacrime di coccodrillo.
examples_en: After firing him, now he's shedding crocodile tears.

back: to leave someone in the lurch, to ditch
definition: Used when someone abruptly abandons a person, a partner or a friend, especially when they need help.
examples: Mi ha piantato in asso proprio il giorno del matrimonio.
examples_en: He left me in the lurch on the very day of the wedding.

back: to take with a grain of salt
definition: Said of news or claims that should be treated with caution because they may not be reliable.
examples: Quella notizia va presa con le pinze.
examples_en: That news should be taken with a grain of salt.

back: to be left empty-handed, to get nothing
definition: Used when someone gets nothing while others receive something, like a missed share of food or reward.
literal: to stay with a dry mouth
examples: Sono arrivato tardi e sono rimasto a bocca asciutta.
examples_en: I arrived late and ended up with nothing.

front: restare con un pugno di mosche
lemma: restare con un pugno di mosche
back: to be left empty-handed
