definition: Used when you end up with nothing after expecting to gain something.
literal: to remain with a fistful of flies
examples: Sperava di vincere il premio, ma è rimasto con un pugno di mosche.
examples_en: He hoped to win the prize but ended up empty-handed.

back: to laugh up one's sleeve; to chuckle to oneself
definition: Used when someone laughs or is amused in secret.
examples: Il nonno rideva sotto i baffi mentre litigavamo.
examples_en: Grandpa was chuckling quietly to himself while we argued.

back: to spoil someone's plans, to throw a wrench in the works
definition: Used when someone ruins plans that were going well.
literal: to break the eggs in the basket
examples: Con la sua telefonata mi ha rotto le uova nel paniere.
examples_en: His phone call threw a wrench in my plans.

back: to keep everyone happy; to have it both ways
definition: Used when someone manages to satisfy two conflicting interests at once.
literal: to save the goat and the cabbages
examples: Ha trovato una soluzione per salvare capra e cavoli.
examples_en: He found a solution that keeps everyone happy.

back: to work extremely hard for something, to go through a lot of trouble
definition: Used when achieving something required enormous effort and difficulty.
examples: Ho sudato sette camicie per finire il progetto.
examples_en: I worked my fingers to the bone to finish the project.

back: to cut ties
definition: Used when you end a relationship or all contact with someone for good.
examples: Ha tagliato i ponti con tutta la sua famiglia.
examples_en: He cut ties with his whole family.

back: all in good time, give it time
definition: Advice to be patient because things need time to develop; also 'dare tempo al tempo'.
examples: Tempo al tempo, vedrai che migliorerà.
examples_en: Give it time, you'll see it will get better.

back: to tighten one's belt
definition: Used when you must cut spending because money is tight.
examples: Con questi prezzi dobbiamo tirare la cinghia.
examples_en: With these prices we have to tighten our belts.

back: to haggle, to bargain
definition: Used when trying to get a lower price, for example at a market.
examples: Al mercato mi piace tirare sul prezzo.
examples_en: At the market I like to haggle.

back: to be stuck-up, to show off
definition: Describes someone who acts conceited or too important.
examples: Dopo la promozione se la tira un sacco.
examples_en: Since his promotion he's been really full of himself.

back: one swallow doesn't make a summer
definition: Warns against drawing general conclusions from a single positive sign.
examples: Hai vinto una partita, ma una rondine non fa primavera.
examples_en: You won one game, but one swallow doesn't make a summer.

front: una volta ogni morte di papa
lemma: una volta ogni morte di papa
back: once in a blue moon
definition: Describes something that happens very rarely.
literal: once every death of a pope
examples: Mio fratello ci viene a trovare una volta ogni morte di papa.
examples_en: My brother visits us once in a blue moon.

back: to come out of it badly battered
definition: Used when someone survives a difficult situation but with heavy losses or damage.
literal: to come out of it with broken bones
examples: Dopo il fallimento, ne è uscito con le ossa rotte.
examples_en: After the bankruptcy, he came out of it badly battered.

front: arrivare come il cacio sui maccheroni
lemma: arrivare come il cacio sui maccheroni
back: to come at just the right moment, to be just what was needed
definition: Describes something or someone that arrives at exactly the right time or fits perfectly.
literal: to arrive like cheese on macaroni
examples: Il tuo aiuto è arrivato come il cacio sui maccheroni.
examples_en: Your help came at exactly the right moment.

back: to have a guilty conscience
definition: Said of someone who gets defensive because they feel guilty about something.
examples: Si è offeso subito: evidentemente ha la coda di paglia.
examples_en: He got offended right away: clearly he has a guilty conscience.

back: don't hold your breath
definition: Short for 'campa cavallo che l'erba cresce'; said when something is unlikely to happen soon.
examples: Aspetti un aumento? Campa cavallo!
examples_en: You're waiting for a raise? Don't hold your breath!

back: to be overjoyed, to be in seventh heaven
definition: Describes someone delighted and blissful, often because of flattery or a pleasant event.
examples: Con tutti quei complimenti era in brodo di giuggiole.
examples_en: With all those compliments, he was on cloud nine.

back: to be a person of firm principles
definition: Describes someone upright, consistent and inflexible in their values. Often 'un uomo / una donna tutto/a d'un pezzo'.
literal: to be all in one piece
examples: Mio nonno era un uomo tutto d'un pezzo.
examples_en: My grandfather was a man of firm principles.

back: to play dumb; to feign indifference
definition: Used when someone pretends not to know or avoids taking sides.
literal: to act like a fish in a barrel
examples: Non fare il pesce in barile, so che sai tutto.
examples_en: Don't play dumb, I know you know everything.

back: to fret, to stew with anger
definition: Describes getting worked up, angry or worried about something, often needlessly.
examples: Non farti cattivo sangue per così poco.
examples_en: Don't get all worked up over so little.

back: out of the blue (usually of bad surprises)
definition: Used when something unexpected, often troublesome, suddenly lands on someone; also 'tra capo e collo'.
examples: Mi è arrivata una multa fra capo e collo.
examples_en: A fine landed on me out of nowhere.

front: non cavare un ragno dal buco
lemma: non cavare un ragno dal buco
back: to get nowhere; to achieve nothing
definition: Used when all your efforts bring no result.
literal: to not get a spider out of the hole
examples: Abbiamo discusso per ore senza cavare un ragno dal buco.
examples_en: We argued for hours and got nowhere.

back: to spend money like water
definition: Describes spending lavishly and carelessly.
examples: Da quando ha vinto alla lotteria, spende e spande.
examples_en: Since winning the lottery, he spends money like water.

front: togliere le castagne dal fuoco a qualcuno
lemma: togliere le castagne dal fuoco a qualcuno
back: to pull someone's chestnuts out of the fire
definition: Used when you solve a difficult problem for someone else, often at your own risk.
literal: to take the chestnuts out of the fire for someone
examples: Ancora una volta ho dovuto togliergli le castagne dal fuoco.
examples_en: Once again I had to bail him out.

back: all talk and no substance, all show
definition: Said of something or someone that looks impressive but has little real substance.
examples: Il suo progetto è tutto fumo e niente arrosto.
examples_en: His project is all show and no substance.

front: avere gli occhi foderati di prosciutto
lemma: avere gli occhi foderati di prosciutto
back: to be blind to what's obvious
definition: Said of someone who fails to notice what is plain to everyone else.
literal: to have eyes lined with ham
examples: Sei cieco? Hai gli occhi foderati di prosciutto!
examples_en: Are you blind? You can't see what's right in front of you!

back: to hold the purse strings
definition: Used for the person who controls the money in a family or organization.
literal: to hold the strings of the purse
examples: In famiglia è mia madre che tiene i cordoni della borsa.
examples_en: In our family my mother holds the purse strings.
